title: Stug
extract:
The Stug is an automatic Grineer pistol that fires  Corrosive blobs that stick to surfaces and explode. A larger and more powerful blob can be formed using consecutive automatic shots or a single charged shot via Alternate Fire.
This weapon can be sold for  5,000.

Characteristics
This weapon deals 100%  Corrosive damage.
Fires blobs that stick to surfaces or embed into enemies, with a lifespan of 1.5 seconds. Blobs can be stacked by consecutively shooting one spot, refreshing the blob duration with each new stack added. After reaching 10 stacks or the lifespan running out, the blob will detonate and deal 75 - 750 damage in a 0.3 - 2.8 meter radius, scaling with the number of stacks. Explosion has 70% damage falloff (despite being listed as 30%), dealing 30% damage at the edge of its radius.
Multishot will not shoot additional blobs, but will instead shoot blobs with an equivalent amount of extra stacks. For example, +100% multishot will cause each blob shot to have 2 stacks, reaching max stacks after only 5 consecutive shots.
Explosions do not self-stagger.
Explosion does not need direct Line of Sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls.
Can benefit from  Fulmination ( Primed).
While stuck to a surface, blobs deal 4 - 36 damage in a 2 meter radius, once immediately upon the blob embedding and then again every second. Damage scales with the number of blob stacks and has 100% damage falloff, dealing 0% damage at the edge of its radius.
Extending the lifespan of a blob by adding stacks to it will allow it to continue dealing this AoE embed damage until the blob finally expires or reaches max stacks.
Alternate Fire charges up a fully (10) stacked blob over 2 seconds, at the cost of 10 ammo.
The alternate fire becomes unavailable while the Incarnon Adapter is installed in the weapon.
Innate  polarity.

Acquisition
The Stug's blueprint can be purchased from the Market.

Notes
Blobs can be stuck to allies.
Blobs will bounce off of Nullifier Crewman shields.

Incarnon Genesis

Upon completion of The Duviri Paradox and Angels of the Zariman, and unlocking The Steel Path, players can earn  Stug Incarnon Genesis from The Circuit's Steel Path to place on their Stug with the help of Cavalero in the Chrysalith. This Incarnon Genesis form grants it evolutions to a transformation and newfound strength.
Purchased from Cavalero for  120, complete with the resources used in its installation. This purchase can only be made once.

Installing the Stug requires 20  Pathos Clamps, 150  Aggristone, and 60  Tasoma Extract.
When installed, the first Evolution tier is unlocked. The following Evolution tiers, their requirements for unlocking them, and their related perks, are shown below;
Each challenge additionally grants 5,000 affinity to the weapon, affected by Affinity Boosters.

Overview
Incarnon Form is charged by filling the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that appears under the reticle by hitting enemies with direct hits and then pressing the Alternate Fire button. 30 direct hits will completely fill the gauge. A full gauge is not required to activate Incarnon Form.
1 Incarnon charge is given on direct hit. 1 charge is given when a blob explodes, but only if the blob is attached to an enemy (charge is only given from the attached target, not surrounding enemies hit by the explosion). 0 charge is given from the embed DoT damage.
Once an enemy is killed, leftover blobs stuck to them will not give charge when they explode.
Shooting additional blobs onto a blob that's already attached to an enemy will still grant 1 charge for each direct hit. However, only 1 total charge will be given for the final blob explosion, regardless of how many blobs are combined.
Because of this, Incarnon charge can be built faster by spreading out shots rather than stacking blobs in one spot. This will allow every shot to grant 2 charges; 1 from the direct hit and 1 from the explosion.
Multishot increases blob size rather than the number of blobs, so it does not increase the number of Incarnon charges gained per blob.
Mode switching is not instantaneous and has an animation equal to the weapon's reload speed.
Swapping to and from Incarnon Form will fully reload the normal form's magazine.
Instead of drawing ammunition from its reserves, the Stug's Incarnon Form uses a separate "magazine" with each charge producing 4 rounds to a maximum of 120. Once all ammunition is expended, the Stug reverts to its normal form.
Incarnon Form's magazine is not affected by mods.
Incarnon Form is not affected by Ammo Efficiency (such as  Energized Munitions).
Charges and Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as holstering, bleedout, or being disarmed. However, charges and Incarnon Form are removed upon death.

Evolutions

Tips
 Barrel Diffusion and  Lethal Torrent will allow the Stug to build up blobs much faster, while Lethal Torrent can increase firing and charging speed of the weapon.
 Fulmination increases the crowd control potential of this weapon, particularly when spreading small blobs all over a room to deal damage against a large crowd of enemies.
The Stug can have three unique combination elementals, with Corrosive already provided, allowing Pathogen Rounds and  Convulsion mods to be equipped separately for such combinations.
The Stug's shots will not just stick to enemies, but other players too. This lets you put them on another player for a little bit of quick melee defense (similar to Vauban's Teslas, but much shorter-lived). Also, the shots will stick to Loki's Decoy and Saryn's Molt for an effective trap.
The innate  polarity can somewhat limit elemental modding potential unless building for  Magnetic,  Blast or  Viral damage, thus making it a less desirable polarity for elemental modding. If you wish to focus more on different elemental damages, then it is recommended to either ignore the polarity or use Forma to turn it into a more suitable polarity.
Charging the alt fire then rapid firing it at a high enough rate of fire (through means of scroll wheel or a macro) will result in all shots from the alt fire maintaining the full charge, allowing for much higher DPS than normal conditions allow.

Bugs
Despite the UI listing the weapon's radial damage falloff as only 30% (dealing 100% - 70% damage over its range), it is actually 70% (dealing 100% - 30% damage over its range), dealing far less damage than intended.

Trivia
The Stug is the third of four very large secondary weapons, the first two being the  Acrid and the  Ballistica, with the  Sepulcrum being the fourth.
"Stug" is likely taken from the WW2 German assault gun of the same name (Sturmgeschütz III & IV); this makes it the second Grineer weapon named after a military vehicle, the first being the  Hind.
This is the second secondary weapon that has a Charge ability.
While the game startup window (the one that lists recent updates) refers to the Stug as a Goo-gun, the shop calls it a Gel gun.
Stug blobs that embed onto the Jackal are unable to deal damage to it.
The weapon strongly resembles the Bio Rifle in Digital Extremes' 1999 game Unreal Tournament. Both weapons fire short-range, slow-moving arcing blobs that stick to surfaces, and both weapons have rapid autofiring as primary fire, and the alternate fire charges a larger blob. While Stug fires white blobs with corrosive damage, the Bio Rifle fires globs of green toxic sludge.
